sections.label: Overview
sections.purpose: Concise scholarly summary of the figure, name, tradition, and significance.
sections.body:
**Psychḗ** ​(*psyche*) ‌— Soul, ‌Breath, ​Life ​· ​Soul, ​breath — ​belongs ‌to ​the ​Greek tradition, ‌where ​it ‌is ​catalogued under ‌the ​domain ​"Soul, ​Breath, ​Life". The ​name ‌means ​"Soul, ‌breath"[^1].

**Psychḗ** ​belongs ‌to ​the ‌Greek ​tradition, where ‌it ​is ​associated ‌with soul, ‌breath, ‌life.[^2]

​PuniCodex ​restores the ‌name ​as ​**Psychḗ** ‌and ​serves its ​temple ‌at ​[psyche.com](https://punicodex.com/psyche/). ‌The original ​carries ​both ​stress ​and ‌vowel length, ‌and ​exactly ‌one ​historically valid ​Unicode ‌restoration ‌exists, ‌which places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier ​1. The ​plain ‌ASCII ​form ​*psyche* survives ​as ‌a ​modern ​convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, is ​the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete[^3].

sections.label: The Name
sections.purpose: Etymology, ASCII constraint, Unicode restoration, name variations, tier classification.
sections.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Greek as ​**Ψυχή**. Etymologically ​it means ​"Soul, breath"[^1].

​The reconstructed ​proto-form is ‌*bʰeyg-* (proto-indo-european, ​"to blow, ​breathe"). ‌Greek ψυχή ​'breath, life, ‌soul'; from ​the verb ‌ψύχω 'to ​blow, to ​cool'. In ​myth, Psyche ​is the ​mortal beloved ‌of ​Eros.

The ‌ASCII form ​*psyche* survives ‌only because ​the early ‌domain-name system ​could not ‌carry diacritics; ​it is ​a technological ‌compromise, ‌not an ‌ancient spelling. ​The Unicode ​restoration **Psychḗ** ‌recovers both ​the stress ​accent and ‌the vowel ​length of ​the original ‌directly ​in the ‌address bar. ​The original ​carries both ​stress and ​vowel length, ‌and exactly ‌one historically ​valid Unicode ‌restoration exists, ​which ​places the ‌name in ‌Tier 1.

‌The letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

​- **p** ‌→ **P** ​— P ​uppercase
- ​**s** → ‌**s** ​— s ​same
- ​**y** → ‌**y** — ​y same
​- **c** ​→ **c** ‌— c ​same
- ‌**h** → ​**h** ‌— h ​same
- ‌**e** → ‌**ḗ** — ​Stress + ​length

The ​canonical temple ​for this ‌name is ‌served at ​**psyche.com**[^2].

sections.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name is ​**/psyche/** ​— ​Greek ‌Reconstruction.[^1]

​Phoneme ​by ‌phoneme:

​- ‌**P** ​— Initial ‌character ​of ​the ​restored ​form ​Psychḗ.
‌- ​**sychḗ** ‌— Remainder ​of ‌the ​name, ‌preserving ​the ‌distinctive ​marks ​of ‌the ‌Greek tradition.

‌For ​the ​modern ‌speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: ​'PSYCHE' ‌— pronounce ​the ‌restored ​form ​with ​attention ​to ‌the ‌preserved ​diacritics ‌and length.

​Kindred ​and ‌historical ‌forms ‌of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Greek** ​— Psychḗ, ​the ‌restored ​Unicode ​form ​of ‌the ​name

​Psychḗ ​is Tier ‌1 ​because ‌the ​Greek ‌form ​preserves ‌distinctive ‌features ​that ​ASCII loses: ​stress, ​length, ‌or ‌special ​characters.

sections.label: Mythology
sections.purpose: Core myths, primary narratives, and textual evidence.
sections.body:
The ​stories of ‌**Psychḗ** ‌circulate within ​the ​Greek corpus, ​where ​the figure ​embodies ‌soul, breath, ​life.[^1]

​### Primary ‌Attestation ​(Sources)

Psychḗ ‌is ​attested in ‌the ​canonical Greek ​sources ​as a ​figure ​associated with ‌soul, ​breath, ‌life.[^2]

### ​Name ‌and Meaning ​(Etymology)

‌The name ​means ‌"Soul, breath" ​and ​reflects the ‌figure's ‌role in ‌the ​tradition. **Psychḗ** ​is ‌the personified ​soul, ​best known ‌from ​Apuleius's *Metamorphoses* ​in ‌the tale ​of ‌Cupid and ​Psyche. ​A mortal ​of ​surpassing beauty, ‌she ‌is forbidden ​to ‌see her ​divine ​husband; when ‌she ‌disobeys, she ‌must ‌perform impossible ​tasks ‌for Venus ​before ​being granted ​immortality.[^1] ‌The ​story allegorizes ​the ​soul's trials ‌on ​the path ​to ​divine union. ‌Psyche's ​tasks—sorting grains, ‌fetching ​golden wool, ‌and ​retrieving beauty ‌from ‌the underworld—are ​trials ​that transform ​her ​from passive ‌beloved ‌into active ​soul.[^2]
